title: Khaman Dhokla
state: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
jainNotes: Contains ginger in the batter. For Jain version, use only green chilli and omit ginger.
description: A popular Gujarati-origin steamed snack made from fermented chickpea batter. Soft, fluffy, and slightly tangy, it is a staple breakfast item across the region, reflecting strong Gujarati culinary influence .
ingredients: 1 tsp Eno/fruit salt or baking soda
Turmeric, sugar, salt, green chilli-ginger paste
Mustard seeds, sesame, curry leaves, green chillies for tempering
steps: Mix besan with yogurt/water, turmeric, sugar, salt and chilli-ginger paste into a smooth batter.
Just before steaming, add Eno and mix gently.
Pour into a greased steaming tray and steam for 12–15 minutes.
Cool slightly and cut into squares.
Temper mustard, sesame, curry leaves and green chillies in oil and pour over the dhokla.
Garnish with coconut and coriander.
Serve with green chutney and sweet tamarind chutney.
tips: Soft, spongy texture comes from the leavening and proper steaming.
A quintessential breakfast and snack item in Gujarati-influenced cuisine.

title: Dal Dhokli
state: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
jainNotes: Contains onion and garlic - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit onion-garlic.
description: A comforting Gujarati-style one-pot meal featuring wheat dumplings cooked in a spiced lentil broth. Widely popular in the region due to strong Gujarati culinary influence, this dish combines earthy lentil flavours with soft, chewy dumplings .
ingredients: Turmeric, red chilli powder, coriander powder, cumin
steps: Pressure-cook toor dal with turmeric.
Prepare a dough with wheat flour, spices, and a little oil.
Roll thin and cut into diamond or square pieces (dhokli).
Bring dal to a boil with water, spices, jaggery, tamarind, and peanuts.
Drop the dhokli pieces in and cook until they are soft and the dal thickens.
Temper with mustard, cumin, curry leaves and hing.
Serve hot.
tips: Comfort food that combines dal and wheat pieces.
Slightly sweet-tangy flavour is characteristic of Gujarati-style cooking.

title: Ubadiyu (Gujarati Barbecue)
state: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
jainNotes: Contains root vegetables (potato, sweet potato, purple yam) and garlic - not consumed by Jains.
description: A local delicacy and seasonal winter dish from South Gujarat and Dadra and Nagar Haveli. Vegetables and beans are slow-cooked in an earthen pot placed upside down over fire, giving it a smoky barbecue-like flavour. Often called the 'Gujarati Barbecue' .
ingredients: Garlic paste, green chilli paste, ginger paste
steps: Make pastes of coriander, garlic, green chilli, ginger, and turmeric .
Wash and cut all vegetables. In a large bowl, mix vegetables with the spice paste .
In a large pressure cooker or pot, add water. Arrange cabbage leaves at the bottom, followed by half of the green stalks .
Evenly spread the marinated vegetables on top. Cover with remaining green stalks .
Cover the pot and place on medium-high heat for 30 minutes, then continue cooking on medium heat until done .
Discard the green stalks when cooked.
Serve hot with green chutney and matho (spiced buttermilk) .
tips: The dish is unique for its fragrance and earthiness from kalar (Indian nettle) and kamboi (black honey shrub) .
Best enjoyed during winter when ingredients are in season .

title: Traditional Fish Curry
state: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
jainNotes: Contains fish and onion - not consumed by Jains.
description: The heart of Daman and Diu's coastal cuisine - freshly caught fish cooked in a coconut-based sauce infused with turmeric, red chilli, and coriander. The balance of heat and flavour with creamy coconut makes this curry rich and satisfying .
ingredients: Fresh fish (seer, pomfret, or local catch)
Turmeric, red chilli powder, coriander powder
steps: Marinate fish with turmeric and salt.
Sauté onion, ginger, and garlic in oil.
Add spice powders and cook until fragrant.
Add tamarind extract and coconut milk, bring to a simmer.
Add fish pieces and cook gently until done.
Garnish with curry leaves and serve with steamed rice.
tips: Fish is a staple food in Daman and Diu, available fresh from the Arabian Sea .
The Portuguese influence adds unique preparation methods distinct from other Indian coastal cuisines .

title: Crab Curry
state: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
jainNotes: Contains crab and onion - not consumed by Jains.
description: A coastal seafood dish popular in Daman and Diu, reflecting the region's Portuguese colonial influence. Fresh crab is cooked in a yellow curry with onion, tomato, garlic, coconut, and spices, prepared in the traditional Indo-Portuguese style common to the coastal territories .
steps: Clean and cut crab into pieces.
Sauté onion, garlic, ginger, and tomato in oil.
Add spice powders and cook until fragrant.
Add crab pieces and cook for a few minutes.
Add coconut milk and simmer for about 30 minutes .
Serve with white rice and papad .
tips: Crab is traditionally eaten by hand to facilitate extraction of meat .
A common dish in Daman and Diu reflecting the Portuguese influence on local cuisine .

title: Patra ni Macchi
state: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
jainNotes: Contains fish and coconut - not consumed by Jains.
description: A celebrated Parsi dish popular in the coastal regions, including Daman and Diu - fresh fish fillets marinated in a vibrant green chutney of coconut, coriander, mint, and aromatic spices, then wrapped in banana leaves and steamed to perfection .
steps: Grind coconut, coriander, mint, green chillies, garlic, and spices into a smooth chutney .
Marinate fish fillets in the green chutney for 30 minutes.
Wrap each fillet in a banana leaf and secure .
Steam until the fish is tender and cooked through .
Serve hot with steamed rice.
tips: The banana leaf wrapping keeps the fish moist and infuses it with a subtle aroma .
Represents the sophisticated seafood preparation influenced by Parsi and Portuguese traditions .

title: Salli Boti
state: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
jainNotes: Contains mutton and onion - not consumed by Jains.
description: A Parsi meat dish popular in the region - tender mutton cooked in a rich, spiced tomato gravy, topped with crispy potato straws (salli). This dish perfectly represents the multicultural Parsi influence in Daman and Diu's cuisine .
steps: Sauté onion and ginger-garlic in oil.
Add tomato and cook until soft.
Add mutton and spice powders, cook until browned.
Add water and slow-cook until mutton is tender.
Finish with garam masala.
Top with crispy potato straws before serving.
Serve with roti or rice.
tips: The crispy potato straws (salli) add a delightful crunch to the rich, tangy gravy .
Combines Persian cooking methods with local ingredients.

title: Vindaloo
state: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
jainNotes: Contains pork and garlic - not consumed by Jains.
description: A Portuguese-influenced dish popular in the coastal territories - pork cooked with garlic, vinegar, and a blend of spices. The name comes from the Portuguese 'vinha d'alhos' (wine and garlic). A classic representation of the Indo-Portuguese culinary fusion found in Daman and Diu.
steps: Grind chillies, garlic, spices with vinegar into a paste.
Marinate pork in the paste for several hours or overnight.
Heat oil, brown onions, add marinated pork.
Cook on medium heat until tender and gravy thickens.
Serve with sannas, pao, or rice.
tips: The Portuguese colonial influence on Daman and Diu's cuisine is strongly reflected in this dish.

title: Bebinca
state: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
jainNotes: Contains eggs - not consumed by Jains.
description: A traditional Portuguese-influenced layered dessert popular in the coastal territories - made with coconut milk, eggs, flour, and sugar. Each layer is baked separately, creating unique textures and flavours. A sweet legacy of the region's Portuguese colonial past.
steps: Mix coconut milk, egg yolks, sugar, flour, and nutmeg into a smooth batter.
In a baking dish, pour a thin layer of batter and bake or grill until set and golden.
Brush with ghee.
Repeat layering and baking until all batter is used (traditionally 7-16 layers).
Cool completely, slice and serve.
tips: A Portuguese legacy still thriving in Daman and Diu's culinary scene .
